aliases: Cholangiocarcinoma of the intrahepatic bile duct
support_spans: a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe
Liver MRI demonstrated an occupying lesion in the right lobe with mild intrahepatic bile duct dilatation, raising the possibility of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
concepts.why: Elevated CA19-9 levels and imaging findings of a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa and intrahepatic bile duct dilatation are suggestive of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

support_spans: a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe
multiple gallstones with gallbladder wall thickening
contradict_spans: Liver MRI demonstrated an occupying lesion in the right lobe with mild intrahepatic bile duct dilatation, raising the possibility of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
concepts.why: Elevated CEA levels and imaging findings of a mass near the gallbladder fossa and gallbladder wall thickening are suggestive of gallbladder cancer.

support_spans: a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe
concepts.why: Elevated AFP levels and imaging findings of a heterogeneous echoic mass in the liver are suggestive of hepatocellular carcinoma, although the elevated CA19-9 levels are not typical for this diagnosis.

support_spans: right upper abdominal tenderness without rebound or palpable masses
multiple gallstones with gallbladder wall thickening
concepts.why: Imaging findings of gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening, along with right upper abdominal tenderness, are suggestive of cholecystitis.

support_spans: a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe
multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes
contradict_spans: no extrahepatic primary tumor was identified
concepts.why: Elevated CEA levels and imaging findings of a mass in the liver and enlarged lymph nodes are suggestive of metastatic liver disease, although no primary tumor was identified.

rationales.F01: Right upper abdominal pain is a common symptom of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and cholecystitis.
rationales.F05: Right upper abdominal tenderness is a common sign of gallbladder disease and liver cancer.
rationales.F07: Negative Murphy's sign and shifting dullness decrease the likelihood of cholecystitis.
rationales.F10: Elevated CA19-9 is a tumor marker for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and other cancers.
rationales.F12: A heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa is highly suggestive of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
